chunks: With this chain of transmission, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about wiping over the feet, how it is. So he placed his palm on the toes, then wiped them up to the ankles. I said to him: If a man were to do it with two fingers of his fingers like this up to the ankles? He said: “No, except with his entire palm.”
And al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, who said:

I wrote to Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام asking him about wiping over the feet, and he said: “Wudu (ablution) is by wiping, and nothing besides that is obligatory in it; and whoever washes, there is no harm.” That means if he intends by it cleaning; this indicates that.

key_terms.التَّنْظِيفَ: cleaning, the non-obligatory intention mentioned for washing
key_terms.الْقَدَمَيْنِ: the two feet, the body part discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الْكَعْبَيْنِ: the ankles, the endpoint of the wipe
key_terms.الْمَسْحِ: wiping as the prescribed act in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification under discussion
key_terms.كَفَّهُ: his palm, indicating the manner of performing the wipe

ai.seo_question: How should the feet be wiped in wudu (ablution) according to Imam Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling of wiping the feet in wudu (ablution), showing that the obligatory act is masḥ, not washing. It also describes the manner of wiping as being done with the whole palm from the toes to the ankles, while washing is tolerated only when intended for cleaning and not as the obligatory form.
